post.caption:
Forgetting is not a failure. Unused connections are pruned on purpose, and people with hyperthymesia who cannot forget describe it as intrusive rather than useful. The genuinely unsettling part is reconsolidation: recalling a memory reopens it, and it goes back down slightly changed by wherever you are now. Which means your most-told story is your least accurate one.
